sections.h2: Which Trumbull County office handles which part of the tax bill?
sections.html:
The Auditor values property and takes homestead applications and Board of Revision complaints. The Treasurer mails bills and collects the money. Both work from the Administration Building at 160 High Street NW in Warren, on the second floor.

  • Auditor: 330-675-2420, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. per its appraisal page. Valuation questions can also go to 330-675-2895.
  • Treasurer: 330-675-2436, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. with no lunch closing, according to its FAQ.
  • Board of Revision forms by email: BOR@co.trumbull.oh.us.

Tax rate cards for every district are posted as PDFs on the Treasurer's tax information page, going back to 2010. The Auditor's records, bills and payment history sit in its online property search, though manufactured home taxpayers must phone the Treasurer because those parcels are not listed there.

sections.h2: What is Trumbull County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Trumbull sits in the far northeast corner of Ohio. Wikipedia notes that it is the only square county in Ohio, roughly 25 miles on a side, with 637 square miles in all. Warren is the seat and largest city. Cortland, Girard, Hubbard and Niles are the other cities, and part of Youngstown reaches in from the south. The county was created in 1800 and once covered the whole Connecticut Western Reserve, with Warren as its first capital. I-80, US 62, US 422 and State Route 11 are the main roads.

Census QuickFacts estimates 198,972 residents for 2025, down 1.5 percent from the 2020 base, and 94,514 housing units. About 71.3 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, the median owner-occupied value is $141,800, median gross rent is $797 and median household income is $56,435. Adults 65 and older make up 24.3 percent of the population, which is why the age-based homestead program matters here. Only 112 building permits were issued in 2025.

sections.h2: When are Trumbull County property taxes due, and how can I pay?
sections.html:
Real estate tax comes due twice a year, generally in March and August, and the exact dates print on each bill. For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the Treasurer posted March 6 and August 31, 2026. Manufactured home dates were March 2 and August 21, 2026. Bills usually go out by the end of January and again by the end of June. A mailed payment counts on its postmark date, and the Treasurer adds that posting can take 7 to 10 days after a collection closes. There is no discount for paying the full year early.

The Treasurer takes payment these ways:

  • Mail a check or money order to the Treasurer at 160 High Street NW, Floor 2A, Warren, OH 44481.
  • Use the 24-hour drop box beside the Administration Building on Harmon Avenue, for checks or money orders only.
  • Pay online from the Auditor's property search by e-check, debit card or credit card.
  • Call 1-833-339-1306 to pay by phone.
  • Visit the counter with cash, check, card or money order.

Processing fees go to the vendor, not the county: $1.00 per e-check and 2.5 percent of the total for cards. A bounced check draws a $15.00 fee. One check can cover several parcels if you list each parcel number on the memo line.

Owners who owe nothing past due can join the Tax Installment Payment Plan, which prepays taxes through monthly coupons. Call the Treasurer and ask for a TIP clerk.

sections.h2: How does the Trumbull County Auditor arrive at my home's value?
sections.html:
The Auditor uses mass appraisal, meaning one standard method applied to a whole universe of parcels, about 144,000 in Trumbull County by the office's count. Staff draw on field checks, aerial photography, owner-supplied sale data such as a settlement statement, local auction results and listing-service data. They usually cannot enter the house. A bank appraisal inspects inside and out for one property, while the mass method leans on exterior review and three years of sales.

Ohio taxes 35 percent of appraised market value, and one mill is $1 per $1,000 of that taxable value. Values refresh countywide every three years, and the 2023 reappraisal is the one the Auditor's guide describes. Voters, not the Auditor, set the voted millage. After a reappraisal, rates adjust so voted levies bring in the same revenue as before, and only inside millage of 10 mills or less moves directly with value. Special assessments for things like ditches, paving, curbs, sewer and water lines, lighting and trash removal ride on the same bill but are not tax.

sections.h2: How do I file a value complaint with the Trumbull County Board of Revision?
sections.html:
The Board of Revision handles value, not the tax dollars. Ohio's complaint window closes on March 31 or at the end of first-half collection, whichever comes later, under R.C. 5715.19. The complainant carries the burden of proof.

Trumbull County Board of Revision steps, from the Auditor's board page
StageWhat happens
Who sitsAuditor, Treasurer and Commissioners, each able to send a representative
FormsDTE 1, 1M or 2 for value; DTE 106B for homestead or owner-occupancy disputes
FilingEmail, mail, fax or in person; handwritten forms need a notary, electronic ones do not
ReviewSome cases get a settlement offer you may accept or reject
Hearing noticeAt least 10 days ahead, in person, by phone or by Webex
EvidencePrefer it with the complaint; give at least 7 days before the hearing
Appeal30 days from the decision letter to the Board of Tax Appeals or Common Pleas

Evidence the board lists as common includes a licensed appraiser's report, photos, repair estimates, and a settlement statement and purchase agreement for a recent sale. A school board may file a counter-complaint within 30 days. The Auditor says taxes stay due while a complaint is pending, and paying in full avoids penalty risk. A reduction comes back as a credit or refund. The board also notes a threshold for complaints after an arm's-length sale: the price must exceed the listed value by ten percent and the state filing threshold, set at $567,000 for tax year 2025.

sections.h2: Which Trumbull County tax reductions can a seller or heir use?
sections.html:
The Auditor's homestead page describes two programs.

  • Homestead exemption: up to $29,000 off market value for owners at least 65, permanently and totally disabled owners, and some surviving spouses who were 59 or older at the time of death. The income cap for 2026 taxes payable in 2027 is $41,000, and the late-application cap for 2025 taxes payable in 2026 is $40,000, measured on Ohio adjusted gross income of owner and spouse.
  • Veterans rated 100 percent permanently disabled from service may receive up to $58,000, with no income cap.
  • Owner-occupancy reduction: close to 2.5 percent off the bill while the owner lives there. The page states there is no application deadline, and it covers the home and one acre.

A denied homestead or owner-occupancy claim can be appealed on form DTE 106B within 60 days of the notice. Late-payment penalties can be remitted on form DTE 23A, filed with the Treasurer, if the Auditor cannot grant the request.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a Trumbull County house sells?
sections.html:
The owner of record when the bill is due owes it, the Treasurer's FAQ says, and the bill carries the name on the deed as of the start of the tax year. The FAQ tells buyers and sellers to read their purchase agreement for who pays what, and to ask the title or mortgage company if unsure, because the Treasurer's Office has no copy of that agreement.

The Auditor's conveyance desk collects $4.00 per thousand of value conveyed plus $0.50 per parcel, and exempt transfers pay only the parcel charge. A deed goes first to the Tax Map office, then the Auditor, then the Recorder, with a legible copy of the last deed of record. Mailed transfers need a self-addressed stamped envelope and a check made out to the Trumbull County Auditors Office.

sections.h2: What if taxes on a Trumbull County house go unpaid?
sections.html:
Tax foreclosure sales run in person every other Thursday at 1:30 p.m. in the Commissioners' hearing room at 160 High St. NW, under rules effective May 7, 2026. Bidding starts at a minimum and rises by $100. The winning bidder posts a $3,000 deposit in certified funds, and the balance is due 30 days after the confirmation of sale. The owner may redeem until the judge signs that confirmation. Mortgage foreclosures moved to an online platform under House Bill 390.

The Trumbull County Land Bank, created in late 2010 through the Treasurer's office, takes vacant and tax-delinquent parcels and markets them for reuse. Its programs are run with Trumbull Neighborhood Partnership. For a house you want to sell before it reaches that stage, ask the title company to request a payoff amount from the Treasurer.

faqs.q: Does Trumbull County honor the postmark on a mailed tax payment?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer says it honors the postmark date for mailed payments, though posting can take 7 to 10 days after collection closes.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying the whole Trumbull County bill early?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer's FAQ says there is no discount for early full payment. The Tax Installment Payment Plan spreads payments through monthly coupons for owners who are current.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax if I sell mid-year in Trumbull County?
faqs.a: The owner of record when the bill comes due owes it. The Treasurer points sellers and buyers to their purchase agreement, which sets who reimburses whom.

faqs.q: Can I appeal if the Auditor denies my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. File form DTE 106B with the Board of Revision within 60 days of the denial notice. Manufactured home owners have until January 31 of the following year.

faqs.q: What card fee does the Trumbull County Treasurer charge?
faqs.a: Card payments carry a 2.5 percent processing fee and e-checks cost $1.00. The vendor keeps that fee, not the county. Cash and checks at the counter avoid it.
